### CVE-2017-5941
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2017-02-09 | Updated: 2024-08-05 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 45265: Node.JS - 'node-serialize' Remote Code Execution (remote/linux, 2017-02-08, verified=0)
- Exploit-DB 49552: Node.JS - 'node-serialize' Remote Code Execution (2) (webapps/nodejs, 2021-02-10, verified=0)
- Exploit-DB 50036: Node.JS - 'node-serialize' Remote Code Execution (3) (webapps/nodejs, 2021-06-18, verified=0)

An issue was discovered in the node-serialize package 0.0.4 for Node.js. Untrusted data passed into the unserialize() function can be exploited to achieve arbitrary code execution by passing a JavaScript Object with an Immediately Invoked Function Expression (IIFE).

### CVE-2017-16119
- Assigner: hackerone | Published: 2018-06-07 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-400 Denial of Service (CWE-400)
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Fresh is a module used by the Express.js framework for HTTP response freshness testing. It is vulnerable to a regular expression denial of service when it is passed specially crafted input to parse. This causes the event loop to be blocked causing a denial of service condition.

Affected:
- HackerOne / fresh node module: affected < 0.5.2

References:
- https://nodesecurity.io/advisories/526 [x_refsource_MISC]
